post.title: 5 Signs Your Brain Keeps Score of the Bad Stuff #shorts
post.description: Send this to the friend who checked all five. Rosa's review: nine compliments and one 'could improve'. Guess which one she rereads at midnight. 1) one bad comment outlives a pile of good ones, 2) you still cringe at awkward moments from years ago, 3) one rude driver ruins your morning, 4) 'we need to talk' means the worst, 5) you reread the mean one. Five times. It isn't a character flaw. In 2001, Roy Baumeister, Ellen Bratslavsky, Catrin Finkenauer and Kathleen Vohs reviewed research across relationships, feedback, emotions, learning and memory in 'Bad Is Stronger Than Good' (Review of General Psychology) and found that bad events, feedback and feelings generally have a bigger impact than equally sized good ones. Their reading: noticing threats was useful for survival, so the brain weights them heavily. Psychologists call it negativity bias. It's a tendency, not a rule. Try reading the nice ones out loud. Comment 'got me' if you've reread a mean comment today. #psychology #shorts #overthinking #negativitybias #selfcompassion
